title: Devilled Eggs
subtitle: Hard-boiled eggs filled with a spiced yolk mayonnaise
excerpt: Hard-boiled eggs halved and filled with a smooth yolk, mayonnaise, mustard, and paprika mixture. A Victorian-era British buffet staple that is as quick to make as it is easy to eat.
sourceNotes: Mrs Beeton, Book of Household Management (1861), Project Gutenberg #10136. Devilled eggs are found in Mrs Beeton under the heading of egg dishes for supper or luncheon. Eliza Acton, Modern Cookery for Private Families (1845), devilled dishes as a category. The term 'devilled' in British cooking refers to a highly seasoned, spiced preparation.

recipe.batchNotes: Scale freely. Make up to 4 hours ahead and refrigerate, loosely covered.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made up to 4 hours ahead. Keep covered in the fridge and dust with paprika just before serving.

content.text: Devilled eggs are halved hard-boiled eggs with the yolks mixed into a smooth, mildly spiced filling and piped or spooned back in. The technique is simple: boil, cool, halve, mix, fill. The filling needs enough mayonnaise to be smooth and enough mustard and vinegar to cut through the richness of the yolk.
Lower {{eggs}} eggs into a pan of boiling water. Cook for exactly 10 minutes. Transfer immediately to a bowl of cold water and leave for 5 minutes.
Peel the eggs and halve them lengthways. Pop the yolks out into a bowl. Keep the white halves flat on a plate.

Mash the yolks until smooth with a fork. Add {{mayonnaise}} of mayonnaise, {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard, {{white-wine-vinegar}} of white wine vinegar, and {{smoked-paprika}} of smoked paprika. Mix until very smooth. Season well.
Spoon or pipe the filling into each white half, slightly mounding it. Dust with a little extra paprika and scatter over snipped chives if using.

rows.symptom: Yolks have a grey-green ring around them
rows.fix: 10 minutes in boiling water is enough. Transfer immediately to cold water to stop the cooking.

rows.symptom: Filling is grainy rather than smooth
rows.cause: Yolks not mashed finely enough before adding the wet ingredients
rows.fix: Push the yolks through a fine sieve before mixing in the mayonnaise. The filling becomes noticeably silkier.

rows.symptom: White halves slide around on the plate
rows.cause: Rounded underside with no flat base
rows.fix: Slice a thin sliver off the bottom of each white half so it sits flat.

rows.symptom: Filling is too loose and falls out
rows.fix: Add the wet ingredients a little at a time and stop when the filling holds its shape when spooned.

content.text: Devilled eggs appear in Victorian cookbooks as a supper or luncheon item. They were grouped with devilled kidneys and devilled bones as highly seasoned preparations. In British cooking, devilled means seasoned with mustard, cayenne, or similar hot spices. The American variation became more elaborate over time. The British version was already a buffet and picnic standby a century before that.
